_comment: GENERATED by scripts/applicability.py. One ledger per phase, beside verdict.json.
An exception records that ONE mechanical rule does not bind ONE subject here, and why.
It is the third evidence of the applicability boundary (untouched | shipped | excepted): a
phase closed with a recorded exception is CLOSED, not incomplete, so the stage resolver can
move past it without anyone stamping a sign-off nobody gave.
The rule set is CLOSED and every one of them is read by a named call site, because a ledger
entry nothing reads is an exception that does not exist. A rule outside it is a hard error
naming what was invented, never a no-op. `applicability.py rules` prints the set - it is
applicability.RULES that decides, and a second copy here is the copy that goes stale.
Every exception is logged to gate-overrides.log through scripts/bypass_log.sh as it is
recorded; one that could not be logged is not recorded at all.
Do not hand-edit: `applicability.py record` owns this file, and `applicability.py check` is
what the resolver and the requirement cap read.
readers: pipeline_state.py @ per phase, resolving the next stage
verifier_precheck.py @ per spec, resolving a stale spec-gate stamp
breaker_gate.py @ per phase, resolving the Breaker obligation
verifier_evidence.py @ per phase, resolving the execution-evidence obligation

exceptions.subject: <n>.<k>-<subslug>
exceptions.reason: <why this rule does not bind here, from the reason file>
